Carta: solo-founded startups rose from 23.7% of new startups in 2019 to 36.3% in H1 2025. Sizes the segment; says nothing yet about the problem.
Cofounder homepage; Pancake, Best AI Co-Founder Tools in 2026

A crowded 2026 category of products that run a solo founder's departments with agents: Cofounder says over 10,650 companies run on it (self-reported); Founderr, AI Cofounders and VenturOS offer agent executive teams. Founders are paying for agent-run operations, which is a workaround for the problem, but none of these claims is observed by us.

Stork.ai and IdeaProof comparison pages; makerstack.co siift review
https://ideaproof.io/versus/dimeadozen-vs-ideaproof

Founders pay for AI idea-validation scores and reports: ValidatorAI (free 0-100 score, paid sessions), IdeaProof (from EUR 19), DimeADozen (free tier, paid reports), Siift (AI-scored validation that grades assumptions by evidence, from about USD 20 per user per month). Prices from third-party and competitor pages, unverified.
Drata, Startup solutions page
https://drata.com/solutions/size/startup

Startups pay for compliance early: Drata claims 8,500+ customers and a startup offer (SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, ISO 42001); third-party estimates put a startup's first SOC 2 on Vanta at roughly USD 10,000 to 20,000 a year plus audit fees. Evidence that founders meet compliance as a late, costly surprise is not yet gathered.
You build a project and no one ever uses it. There is no strategy for it; you want it to go further but don't know the right next step.

A venture faces many decisions, and there is no framework for knowing all the decisions you will need to make over time, or which are the most consequential right now: what is signal and what is noise.
You have an idea and feel it is good, but you don't know how to research it to prove that it is.
You don't know how to communicate the idea to the right people: a technical professional, an investor and the target audience each need it told differently.

Everyone can build now, but not everyone is a marketer, a salesperson, a financial expert, a storyteller who can inspire a team, or a team builder; a founder may fear losing control of their idea by inviting a cofounder.
Solo founders and small early-stage teams (Discovery or Validation), low- to no-code, building AI-native with agents as editors (EE-045)

Many more people can now build their ideas, but building is no longer the hard part: knowing the right next decision is. Founders lose traction, can't tell the highest-signal decision from the noise, don't know how to prove or communicate their idea, and lack the skills a venture needs beyond building (Torian, 2026-10-28).

Many more people are now able to build applications and build their ideas (Torian, 2026-10-28), so the bottleneck moves from building to deciding. Supporting trend: solo-founded startups rose from 23.7% to 36.3% of new startups, 2019 to H1 2025 (Carta).
